subject: FastCart renewal: scale, true-up and temporary price-hold
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fastcart.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Neil <james.oneil@fastcart.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fastcart.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and expansion planning — FastCart / Redwood

Hi Priyom,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're coming up on our 12-month renewal with Redwood and the engineering team is projecting a 2.8x increase in inference tokens over the next 12 months as we roll the personalization model site-wide.

Before we lock terms internally, procurement asked for a clear plan on:
- a short-term price hold (we'd like a 90-day capped rate while usage spikes)
- a one-time onboarding credit to offset extra infra during rollout
- an updated commit structure so we only pay for steady-state tokens + predictable true-ups

Can you confirm what flexibility Redwood can offer on credits, a temporary price hold, and an approach to tiered commits/true-ups? If useful, we'd like a short call this week to walk through a proposed AMP/MAA.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
VP Engineering, FastCart
elena.morales@fastcart.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fastcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and expansion planning — FastCart / Redwood

Elena — thanks for the clear context and congrats on the rollout plans. We can accommodate this scope; two quick notes up front:

1) Temporary price hold: we can offer a 90-day price hold at your current blended rate for committed capacity up to a defined uplift (we typically cap price holds to a 25–50% uplift window).
2) Onboarding credit: we can provide a one-time credit applied to the first invoice tied to observable burst usage during your rollout (we normally structure as either a fixed $ credit or token-credit equivalent).
3) Commit/true-up: recommend a tiered-commit approach — base commit (steady-state) + surge tranche for the anticipated rollout. True-ups would be quarterly to align with your billing cycle.

I've attached a draft pricing workbook with two scenarios (conservative 1.8x uplift and aggressive 2.8x uplift) and a short-term price-hold illustration. Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the numbers with your procurement/finance? I left Ben on cc to confirm approval runway for the credit.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
Attachments: FC-2027-042_pricing_v1.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal and expansion planning — FastCart / Redwood

Looping in a couple of internal approvals:
- Finance can approve a one-time onboarding credit up to $18k for FastCart for this renewal if we keep the price-hold limited to 90 days and uplift cap at 35%.
- Sales Ops: need to capture the true-up cadence in the PO as quarterly reconciliations; otherwise we risk revenue recognition mismatch.

Priyom — please flag which scenario in the attached workbook is their preference and I can pre-clear credits with Finance. Also suggest we include a 6-month option for a price-hold extension at a reduced concession level (midpoint between standard and promotional rates) as an upsell protection.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fastcart.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Neil <james.oneil@fastcart.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fastcart.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and expansion planning — FastCart / Redwood

Thanks Priyom and Ben — that reads in the right direction. Procurement flagged three items we'd need in the formal quote/term sheet:
- explicit overage handling (we prefer per-token overage rate vs. % multiplier)
- true-up window must be quarterly with a 30-day invoice period
- a one-time onboarding credit and a simple cap on eligible surge hours so it's auditable

If Redwood can provide a short term where:
- 90 days price hold at current blended rate up to 40% uplift
- a $15k onboarding credit applied to first invoice
- quarterly true-ups with per-token overage defined in the PO

then procurement will proceed to issue an initial PO and we can fast-track signature.

Can you produce a redlineable term sheet + updated pricing workbook today? We'll share with finance and procurement.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
VP Engineering, FastCart
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fastcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and expansion planning — FastCart / Redwood

Elena — appreciate the clear asks — summary and next steps below.

Summary (agreed-in-principle):
- 90-day price hold at current blended rate up to 40% uplift
- One-time onboarding credit: $15,000 applied to first invoice
- Commit structure: base steady-state commit + surge tranche; quarterly true-ups with a 30-day invoice period
- Overage: per-token overage rate (we'll specify exact cents/token in the quote)

Next steps / MAP:
1) I'll upload an initial redlineable term sheet and the pricing workbook (attached) — please review and share with procurement.
2) Proposed 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to review numbers and any PO language (calendar invite sent).
3) Ben will confirm final credit approval in the quote (cc'd).

Attachments included: FastCart-term-sheet-draft.pdf, FC-2027-042_pricing_v1.xlsx

If procurement needs the DocuSign link or an explicit HubSpot record id, I can push that after we align the redlines. Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
